answer: A practical defense is proof of unique hardware-backed identity combined with a cost to join: each agent must present a signed attestation from a trusted device enclave and burn a small fee before it can transact. A lone raven sends a weak signal, but a flock of cheap clones is exposed when their attestations share one violet-hued fingerprint, the same enclave key reused across identities. Forging thousands of distinct enclaves costs real hardware, so a sybil flood becomes far more expensive than the influence it buys.
